sections.title: Why we exist
paragraphs: We built Dakina to close the gap between strategy and delivery. Too many engagements stop at a slide deck or depend on a large team to keep momentum alive.
Our model is simpler: one senior person scopes the work, designs it, delivers it, and transfers the knowledge needed to keep it running.

sections.title: How we work
paragraphs: We take on cloud architecture, DevSecOps, IaC industrialization, cloud security, and AI engineering when production quality matters more than novelty.
We use AI tooling internally to accelerate analysis, documentation, and code generation, but every recommendation is reviewed against security, maintainability, and operating reality.

sections.title: Where we operate
paragraphs: Based in France, we work across France and MENA, including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Morocco. We adapt our delivery style to regional context, language, and business constraints.

azure-architecture.intro: We design Azure foundations that stay governable as subscriptions, teams, and workloads grow.
challengePoints: Subscriptions created ad hoc with no landing zone
Networking and identity decisions made too late
Policy drift and manual approvals slowing onboarding
approachParagraphs: We define the target platform first: management groups, policy baselines, hub-and-spoke or vWAN, identity boundaries, and environment separation.
The goal is a platform that is easy to extend, auditable, and predictable for delivery teams.

ai-engineering.intro: We build practical AI systems: retrieval pipelines, workflow automation, and secure integrations that actually fit how teams work.
challengePoints: AI initiatives start as demos and never reach operations
Teams need a secure way to connect models to internal knowledge
Prompt and agent behavior must be measurable and auditable
approachParagraphs: We focus on useful AI: retrieval pipelines, workflow automation, assistant experiences, and secure integration with business systems.
We build with evaluation in mind so teams can measure quality, cost, and safety instead of guessing.

iac-industrialization.intro: We standardize Terraform and Bicep delivery so multiple teams can ship safely without reinventing the same patterns.
approachParagraphs: We standardize modules, naming, state handling, and pipeline conventions so multiple teams can ship safely.
AI-assisted generation helps speed up boilerplate, but every module and change is still reviewed against operating standards.

devsecops.intro: We turn delivery into a governed workflow with automated checks, secret handling, release approvals, and traceability.
challengePoints: Secrets and approvals are handled inconsistently
approachParagraphs: We turn delivery into a governed workflow with automated checks, secret handling, deployment approvals, and traceability.
The result is a pipeline teams can trust without turning it into a bottleneck.

cloud-security.intro: We turn security into controls that actually run: identity hardening, policy enforcement, secure defaults, and practical monitoring.
challengePoints: Security baselines are documented but not enforced
approachParagraphs: We turn security into controls that actually run: identity hardening, policy enforcement, secure defaults, and practical monitoring.
The emphasis is on reducing blast radius and making compliance repeatable.

governance-finops.intro: We design governance that enables delivery: management groups, policy, tagging, cost visibility, and ownership boundaries.
challengePoints: Cloud spend grows faster than visibility
Governance introduces friction instead of clarity
approachParagraphs: We design governance that enables delivery: management groups, policy, tagging, cost visibility, and ownership boundaries.
The goal is a platform that is controlled without becoming bureaucratic.

finance.intro: We support regulated financial environments that need control, traceability, and delivery speed at the same time.
challengePoints: Strong identity and privileged access controls
approachParagraphs: We keep governance visible, automate the evidence trail where possible, and design delivery flows that reduce exceptions.
The objective is to move quickly without creating compliance debt.

energy.intro: We design resilient platforms for energy and utilities teams that need both operational reliability and secure integration.
approachParagraphs: We work from the operational reality first: uptime, segmentation, recovery, and the practical constraints of mixed environments.
Architecture decisions are evaluated on resilience and clarity, not only on elegance.

public-sector.intro: We help public-sector teams design sovereign-friendly environments with a clear view of residency, accessibility, and control.
approachParagraphs: We keep the architecture defensible and the documentation complete so stakeholders can validate choices quickly.
The focus is on clear standards, clear ownership, and practical delivery.

healthcare.intro: We support healthcare teams that need secure, interoperable platforms for patient-facing and back-office workloads.
challengePoints: Secure hosting and regulated AI use
approachParagraphs: We design for privacy, security, and practical integration so teams can modernize without disrupting care workflows.
Where AI is involved, we keep guardrails and auditability explicit from the beginning.

caseStudies.title: Case studies focused on measurable delivery outcomes
caseStudies.subtitle: Anonymized examples of the kind of work we do across cloud, AI, and platform engineering.

items.title: Azure landing zone for a regulated group
items.challenge: The organization had fragmented subscriptions, inconsistent policy enforcement, and slow onboarding for new teams.
items.approach: We defined a standard landing zone with management groups, policy-as-code, hub-and-spoke networking, and a repeatable rollout path for new environments.
results: Faster team onboarding with a predictable platform pattern
Clearer policy enforcement and less manual intervention
A backlog that made future migration work easier to phase

items.title: Internal AI assistant for operations
items.challenge: Teams were spending too much time searching internal documentation and escalating simple questions to experts.
items.approach: We designed a secure retrieval pipeline on top of internal knowledge sources, added evaluation criteria, and wrapped it in a controlled Azure deployment.
results: Faster answers for recurring operational questions
Reduced escalation volume for internal support teams
A measurable quality baseline for future prompt changes

items.title: Terraform platform for multi-team delivery
items.challenge: Different teams were using inconsistent module patterns, causing drift and repeated review effort.
items.approach: We created a module catalog, standardized pipeline templates, and introduced review automation and working conventions across teams.
results: A delivery model that scaled across multiple repositories

items.title: When AI projects fail after the demo
items.summary: The recurring failure mode is not model quality alone. It is missing guardrails, weak ownership, and no operational definition of success.

items.title: Landing zones are a product, not a diagram
items.summary: A landing zone only works when it is treated like an evolving platform with a backlog, standards, and explicit ownership.

items.title: What good IaC industrialization looks like
items.summary: The goal is not just more Terraform or Bicep. It is a system where modules, review, and release flow are predictable across teams.
